metadata.description: BH/BY-FDR correction of the 36-group recovery-time-ratio bootstrap tests, a 3x3 CoV-threshold sensitivity grid re-simulated on the win-corner cell only, an analytical + microbenchmarked per-request compute-cost comparison, a documented short-reset-ablation gap, a real-Twitter-trace steady-state parity + exploratory changepoint check, a reconciled single memory-overhead figure, and one final non-hedged verdict.

tier multipliers are {2, 8, 32} (TIERS), vs baseline's single TUNED multiplier in {4,8,16,32}", "note_on_ewma_not_plain_cov": "method.py does NOT recompute CoV from a full pass over stored history; it maintains an EWMA of the gap and gap^2 (EWMA_ALPHA=0.3) and derives var = max(E[gap^2] - E[gap]^2, 0), cov = sqrt(var)/E[gap] incrementally on every access, which is why classify_ops above is O(1) rather than O(history length)."}, "microbenchmark": {"n_calls": 100000, "n_repeats": 5, "baseline_seconds_mean": 0.1781057335436344, "baseline_seconds_std": 0.004334187769162722, "proposed_seconds_mean": 0.379532340914011, "proposed_seconds_std": 0.009068488853625881, "wallclock_ratio_proposed_over_baseline": 2.130938366568804, "caveat": "Wall-clock ratio is a DISTINCT measurement from the analytical op-count ratio above; branch prediction, cache locality (bytearray vs OrderedDict/tuple allocation), and Python object overhead can make them diverge. Both are reported rather than only the more favorable one."}}

{"present_in_artifact": false, "gap_statement": "ABSENT. The experiment artifact (art_gQEGVMwa8ZKC) records exactly two estimator variants per phaseB cell \u2014 'baseline' (GlobalResetFrequencyEstimator, tuned sample-size multiplier per (ratio, alpha) from Phase A) and 'proposed' (PerKeyDecayFrequencyEstimator). No short-tuned/short-reset baseline variant was run, and metadata.deviations_from_plan contains no note about one being added. Per the plan's own instruction to state this as a gap rather than invent numbers: this comparison (baseline-original / baseline-short-tuned / proposed recovery times in the win-corner cells) CANNOT be reported. What the experiment DOES already establish that bears on the same question: Phase A already tunes the baseline's sample_size_multiplier per (ratio, alpha) by sweeping {4, 8, 16, 32} and picking the best steady-state hit ratio (NOT the fastest recovery), so the existing baseline is tuned for a different objective than 'match the proposed estimator's drift adaptation speed' \u2014 a short-reset ablation aimed specifically at recovery speed was never attempted and remains open."}
